items.criterion: Use NASA’s website as the source of truth (no sign-in/registration)
items.description: Rely on information from NASA-controlled pages (nasa.gov or official NASA subdomains) to determine the next planned Artemis mission and its details. Full credit if the agent uses NASA pages and does not sign in/register. Full credit also if the agent attempts to use NASA.gov but access is blocked/down (e.g., CAPTCHA, outage) and the agent clearly reports the limitation. Partial credit if the agent references non-NASA sources only as secondary context while still treating NASA as authoritative.

items.criterion: Identify the next planned Artemis mission and report required mission details
items.description: Correctly determine which Artemis mission is the next planned/upcoming one according to NASA’s website and report: (1) mission name, (2) planned launch year (or NASA-stated target/window with the year), (3) destination, and (4) primary objective as NASA describes it. Full credit if all four fields are correctly captured from NASA pages. If NASA presents ambiguous/updated information across pages (e.g., differing target dates), full credit if the agent notes the discrepancy and reports the most recently published/most clearly designated 'next' mission details. Partial credit if the agent identifies the correct next mission but one or more fields are missing/overly vague. No credit if the mission selected is clearly not the next planned one per NASA.

items.criterion: Stop after recording the required mission details
items.description: Stop promptly after obtaining and reporting the mission name, planned launch year, destination, and primary objective. Full credit if the agent stops once the required information is recorded, allowing minimal additional navigation only to resolve ambiguity or confirm a conflicting detail on NASA.gov. Partial credit if the agent continues browsing beyond what is reasonably needed but still provides the correct required details.
